doc.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Jazz Composers Orchestra at Newport
summary: After the Guild broke up, she and Michael Mantler kept the orchestra and played Newport where audiences hated it and Billy Taylor refused to announce it.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Ok. Umm and the Jazz Composers Orchestra, did that come out of that or?
Yeah it did , because it originally was called the Jazz Composers Guild Orchestra.

And so me and Michael Mantler used everybody in the whole guild in the orchestra. And, it was just something that you did, you played in the orchestra if you were in the guild. But, uhh, when the guild fell through, six months later.... arguing all the time, people just screamed. And uhh, me and Mike wanted to keep the orchestra going, that was what we were doing, now writing for a big band. Or, he... it was called orchestra but it’s a big band. No it wasn’t, it was two of everything. It was like Noah’s Ark! Michael Mantler decided what it was going to be and I just wrote for it. And we wanted to keep writing for it so we kept it going. We played it actually in Newport with the Jazz Composers Orchestra with the word “Guild” missing... three, four months after the guild broke up.
And you said at Newport, the Newport Jazz Festival?
George Wein? Ok. And how was it received?
Oh, terrible! Everybody hated it. It was horrible.
Umm, it was... pretty much sounded like a bunch of dogs getting caught by the pound or something. It was... we were just crazy, screaming people.

And, um, I remember Milford Graves was the drummer, he played like he played with everybody, he played great. Umm, he didn’t scream. It’s the saxophones, those damn saxophones. I didn’t scream, I just tried to, you know, fit in a note once in awhile when it seemed appropriate. And, that was... Billy Taylor refused to announce it. It was... we were so awful.

Billy Taylor refused to announce it. They had to get somebody else that was unknown to announce it. We were totally regarded with no great esteem. But neither was Sun Ra, he was just... people would say “what? what kind of outer space music is that?”
And Sun Ra loved that, “Oh boy outer space, is that what it sounds like? Whoo! That’s good.”
